newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 4.

text.p: - United States President Bill Clinton will definitely join other heads of state for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit in November. This was an assurance given by the new U.S. ambassador to the Philippines Thomas Hubbard. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday ordered the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority to reevaluate within 15 days the bid of the International Container Terminal Services Inc for the development and operation of Subic Bay Port. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Philippine government is asking the World Bank to provide political risk guarantees to investors who would be chosen as concessionaires for the privatization of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage Systems. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The government has devised a new set of proposals to include taxes from the motor vehicle industry in the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Canada's industry minister John Manley will visit the Philippines starting Wednesday to kick off the first segment of a tour of three Asian countries. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The Securities and Exchange Commission has given government financial institutions approval to go ahead with a stockholders agreement with tobacco magnate Lucio Tan. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)

- International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) is ready to invest $350 million in investments if it is allowed to operate the Subic Container Port, ICTSI chairman Enrique Razon Jr said. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Philippines is being considered by two Silicon Valley firms, 3Com Corp and Solectron, as a possible site to put up integrated operations in the Asia-Pacific region, trade and industry secretary Cesar Bautista said. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission is studying a proposal to set up an overseas Filipino investors programme to allow some five million Filipino overseas and contract workers to invest in the stock market. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
